qualitative_findings: All four scalar channels have their largest800-to1600 differences after0.1s: yaw0.1475s,roll0.12875s,sideslip0.13s,bank0.135s. The error is not confined to the first0.01s.

Complete scaled motion reaches its largest difference at0.0675s: beam2,t=-7.5,spatial rotation_y (tailplane tip). For0.1<t<=1 its largest difference is at0.1875s: beam3,t=5,spatial rotation_z (upper fin tip).
Fine yaw absolute peak decreases from0.0046199763 at0.05125s to decile maxima near0.003 after0.3s, with persistent fluctuations rather than monotonic decay.

Fine roll has a substantial early positive peak0.0013788064 at0.105625s and a later slightly larger peak0.0014110712 at0.766875s; late decile maxima remain about0.00135-0.00141. This is not a startup-only spike or a monotone decay.
Sideslip and bank magnitude increase toward their largest saved values at1s; their early sign-changing oscillations give way to slower drift. This does not by itself establish an unstable mode.
Fine complete-motion norm peaks at0.395625s then its decile maximum decreases through1s; different components can control that norm.
Time-band ratios use their own explicitly recorded fine-grid reference norm. Very small early norms explain the large early percentages; no floor, reweighting, or acceptance change is applied.

Original full-time differences, norms and ratios reproduce exactly. Four of five original0.5% criteria still fail; only bank passes. No new simulation, factorization, solve, matrix product or timestep was performed.
time_band_diagnostic.acceptance: Original full-time0.5% gate unchanged; time bands are descriptive.

historical_output_cost.caveat: Gross removable value bytes before small reference-key overhead; no encoder implemented or benchmarked. Values were independently equality-checked. Numerical chart values, coefficients and acceptance metadata are retained.
historical_output_cost.chronology: Historical cost receipt predates the newly measured C16 run. Its then-unmeasured statement is preserved as historical evidence.

caveats: The bridge dispatch itself was not invoked; only its exact JSON encoder options were applied to the final saved native result.
Duplicate bytes are gross replaceable value bytes before reference-key/schema overhead; no new encoder was implemented.
No estimate of browser memory, transfer time, garbage collection or stall causation follows from these sizes.
The historical Dae48 measurements and their receipt remain unchanged.

evidence.raw: All current stage raw states, BDF residual packets, snapshots, restarts, full seven-grid linear states, source, plans, retained preparation/failure evidence and final receipts.
evidence.old_archives: Historical repository ZIPs are not duplicated; their paths and hashes are retained and they are required separately for those historical claims.

limitations: Coarse same-grid agreement does not establish continuous-time accuracy or nonlinear amplitude convergence.
The temporal 0.5% criterion remains failed for yaw, roll, sideslip and full scaled motion at the finest saved pair; bank alone passes.
No nonlinear fine-grid or half-amplitude case was executed. No inferred acceptance from the coarse metrics.
Native CPU/RSS/output-size measurements are case-specific. Browser performance and the cause of the reported browser stall were not measured.
No production equations/defaults, browser code, build, WASM or hosted release changed. The historical Daedalus near-1-Hz Bode mismatch remains unresolved.
next: Implement lossless trajectory/checkpoint storage against these exact saved data; verify exact round trips and browser resume without dropping steps, precision, physical values or restart metadata, and without changing dt or equations.
Separately study efficient, accuracy-controlled transient integration before repeating fine nonlinear/amplitude convergence cases.
Preserve the unresolved full-aircraft Bode discrepancy and accepted component evidence; do not fit parameters or claim reference parity.
